business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1)
business_model.claim: Euronet sells electronic payment and transaction processing to financial institutions, retailers, service providers and individual consumers, through its own global payments network, platforms and technologies.
quotes: Euronet is a leader in electronic payment and transaction processing solutions for Financial Institutions, Retailers, Service Providers, and Individual Consumers utilizing our global payments network, platforms, and technologies.

business_model.claim: The company reports three segments. In 2025 they contributed about 30% (EFT Processing), 28% (epay) and 42% (Money Transfer) of consolidated revenues. In May 2026 EFT Processing was renamed Payments Infrastructure and Money Transfer was renamed Cross-Border Payments. Only the names changed.
quotes: We operate in the following three segments as of December 31, 2025:

In May 2026, the Company changed the name of the EFT Processing Segment to Payments Infrastructure and the name of the Money Transfer Segment to Cross-Border Payments in order to more accurately reflect the products and services provided by these segments.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A segment descriptions
business_model.claim: The segment mix has shifted. In the latest quarter Payments Infrastructure was about 38% of revenues, epay 25% and Cross-Border Payments 37%. Over the nine months the shares were 34%, 27% and 39%.

Payments Infrastructure (the ATM and POS segment) earns recurring management fees, transaction fees, surcharges and foreign-exchange margin on dynamic currency conversion (DCC), and it also sells software.
quotes: The primary sources of revenues generated by our ATM network are recurring monthly management fees, transaction-based fees, surcharges, and margins earned on DCC transactions.

business_model.claim: Segment revenue growth depends on ATM count and higher-value cross-border transactions, not on raw transaction volume. The 10-K for 2025 shows transactions of 15,534 million versus 11,424 million, but revenue per transaction fell from $0.10 to $0.08 as low-value digital transactions grew.
quotes: The decrease in revenue per transaction is due to an increase in processing digital transactions with a high volume and a low value per transaction.

business_model.claim: Payments Infrastructure revenue grew in the latest quarter on merchant acquiring, Ren software sales and the CoreCard acquisition. Weaker international travel spending, which lowers ATM cash withdrawals, partly offset this.
quotes: Constant currency revenue growth was driven by continued growth in merchant acquiring, Ren sales, and the fourth quarter 2025 acquisition of CoreCard, partially offset by continued economic pressures on discretionary travel spend which negatively affects international ATM cash withdrawals.

business_model.claim: epay earns commissions and processing fees from mobile operators and from distributing digital content, vouchers and gifts through retail point-of-sale terminals. Digital media content is now about 77% of epay revenues, up from about 73% in the 10-K.
quotes: are primarily derived from commissions or processing fees received from mobile phone operators for the processing and distribution of prepaid mobile airtime and commissions earned from the distribution of other electronic content, vouchers, and physical gifts.

business_model.claim: epay is a thin-margin, volume business. Its cost of revenue is mainly commissions paid to retailers, which were $891.8 million against revenues of $1,187.6 million in the 10-K year.
quotes: Direct operating costs primarily consist of the commissions paid to retail merchants for the distribution and sale of prepaid mobile airtime and other prepaid products

business_model.claim: Cross-Border Payments (formerly Money Transfer) earns transaction fees plus the spread between wholesale and retail foreign-exchange rates. Agent and correspondent commissions are its main direct cost.
quotes: are primarily derived from transaction fees, as well as the margin earned from purchasing foreign currency at wholesale exchange rates and selling the foreign currency to customers at retail exchange rates.
Sending and correspondent agents each earn fees for cash collection and distribution services, which are recognized as direct operating costs at the time of sale.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the statements; the explanation is partly inferred from the segment commentary
growth_thesis.claim: Revenue growth is currently not converting into profit growth. Third-quarter revenues were 1,161.1 (table in millions) against 1,145.7, while operating income fell to 171.6 from 195.0 and selling, general and administrative expense rose to 99.0 from 84.6. Growth needs costs to be contained as revenue rises.
quotes: Adjusted EBITDA and operating income were impacted by continued cost inflation.

growth_thesis.claim: Management lowered its full-year outlook to approximately $4.375 billion of revenue, approximately $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of approximately 10%. This implies that growth is expected to continue but at a lower level than the targets set in May. It rests on Cross-Border Payments pressure and currency rates not worsening.
quotes: We now expect approximately $4.375 billion of revenue, approximately $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of approximately 10%.
